inspiration: Monster families use numbered tiers (Kraken 1 to 3, Juggernaut 1 to 3, Snowflake 1 to 3, Krill 1 to 4). Each family grows, so the player learns one design language and reads the tier from the silhouette.

A monster body hands itself over to a ship design on the first turn: an effects group creates the design and destroys the body (SH_JUGGERNAUT_1_BODY.focs.txt, effects block). A swap like this lets a body and its ship form be authored separately.
Monster hulls define external, core and internal slots (SH_JUGGERNAUT_1_BODY.focs.txt). Mark a creature's weak points with slot positions so the player can target the core.
Nest icons (icons/specials_huge/kraken-nest.png and the juggernaut and snowflake nests) show a spawner as a visible world object. A nest that spawns a creature family is a clear zone feature.

Wild krill are described as appearing in systems with asteroid belts (stringtable entry SP_KRILL_SPAWNER, default/stringtables/en.txt:14226). Spawns tied to a terrain feature give a readable reason for an enemy to appear.
Hazard zones are overlay art in default/data/art/fields/ (ion storm, void rift, nanite swarm). A translucent overlay with a distinct colour per hazard is cheap and readable.

briefs.label: Spawner nest
briefs.rule: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
briefs.why: A stationary nest makes the spawn source a place the player can hunt.
briefs.keep: Stationary object; spawns a creature family on a timer; visible from the map
briefs.change: A hive tower or egg cluster instead of a nest; different colour and growth stages; spawn trigger is a player action, not a timer

briefs.label: Three-stage grower
briefs.rule: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
briefs.why: A creature that visibly grows through three stages gives a clear escalation curve.
briefs.keep: Three stages in one family; family-level name; each stage is its own authored body
briefs.change: Each stage a different silhouette, not just bigger; new limb or shell per stage; the family uses a different material. Note: SH_JUGGERNAUT_1_BODY only shows a turn-1 body-to-ship swap; the stage trigger for tiers 2 and 3 was not read

briefs.label: Asteroid-belt swarm
briefs.rule: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
briefs.why: A swarm that spawns only near a terrain feature gives a readable reason to appear.
briefs.keep: Spawns tied to one terrain type; small units in a group; one swarm per feature
briefs.change: A drone swarm with a different movement pattern; a crystal feature instead of an asteroid belt

briefs.label: Crystal snowflake boss
briefs.rule: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
briefs.why: A crystalline boss in a family of three reads as a tier-up of the same enemy.
briefs.keep: Crystal or ice silhouette; family tier numbering; a psionic variant at the top tier
briefs.change: Make it a glassy or salt-crystal form; a different palette; a different signature sound

briefs.label: Ion-storm hazard overlay
briefs.rule: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
briefs.why: A translucent overlay in a distinct colour marks a hazard zone without text.
briefs.keep: Translucent overlay; distinct colour per hazard; sits on the map tile
briefs.change: Use a sand or dust overlay, not a storm; a different shape and motion
